modgee

Estimate extinction from species detection histories with MODGEE (Matrix-Of-Detections-Gives-Extinction-Estimates).

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("zhizhouhe2006/modgee")

The package contains C++ code. Installing from source on Windows requires Rtools compatible with your R version.

Quick start 

library(modgee)

# Prepare detections without overwriting the installed examples.
M <- read_matrix(example_file, timestep = 10, baseline_min_species = 10)
set.seed(123)
result <- fit_modgee(M)
result$summary
plot_modgee(result)
save_result(result, path = "results", prefix = "analysis")

Input rows represent species and columns represent equally spaced numeric time labels. Entries must be 0 or 1. Row and column names are required.

Grouped models and k comparison 

set.seed(123)
result_grouped <- fit_modgee(
  M = example_M, groups = example_groups,
  reference_group = "primary + old secondary", do_k = TRUE
)
result_grouped$group_results$summary
result_grouped$do_k
plot_modgee(result_grouped)

Bootstrap confidence intervals 

set.seed(123)
result_bootstrap <- fit_modgee(
  M = example_M, groups = example_groups,
  reference_group = "primary + old secondary", bootstrap = 200, CI = 0.95
)
plot_modgee(result_bootstrap)
save_result(result_bootstrap, path = "results", prefix = "bootstrap")

Bootstrap refits models and may take substantial time. Checkpoints are stored under modgee_bootstrap in the working directory. Rerun the same call there to resume. Inspect convergence and valid replicate counts before interpreting the intervals.

Precomputed examples

The package provides example_file, example_M, example_groups, example_result, example_grouped_result and example_bootstrap_result. The result objects are precomputed; viewing or plotting them does not refit models. The bootstrap example uses only 10 replicates for demonstration.

plot_modgee(example_bootstrap_result)
save_result(example_bootstrap_result, path = "results", prefix = "example")

CSV exports

save_result() writes summary.csv, time_result.csv and species_result.csv, with the requested prefix. It additionally writes k_comparison.csv when a k comparison is present and CI.csv when bootstrap curve intervals are present. Overall and group results share the same files. Existing files are protected unless overwrite = TRUE.

Documentation and development

See ?read_matrix, ?fit_modgee, ?plot_modgee and ?save_result for argument and output definitions.

devtools::test()
devtools::check()

Scripts in data-raw/ regenerate example datasets; ordinary installation does not need to run them.
